parts: Yes, and another option would be to write a user-defined "distribution" that returns -log(lambda) as the log probability "density", both in quotes because of the impropriety.
On Fri, Sep 25, 2020 at 11:27 AM Simon Bonner <sbon...@uwo.ca> wrote:

Hi Fang,

You can do this by defining a new variable, say log_lambda, assigning log_lambda a flat prior with dflat(), and then setting lambda = exp(log_lambda). 

However, note the warning in the nimble manual that: " y improper prior distributions ... should only be used when the posterior distribution of the model is known to be proper".

Cheers,

Simon
